af.flag: Three vertical stripes — black, red and green — with a white emblem of a mosque and wheat sheaves in the middle.
af.fun: The Wakhan Corridor in the north-east is a narrow strip drawn on the map on purpose, so Russian and British lands would never touch.

ao.flag: Red and black bands with a yellow emblem: half a cog, a machete and a star. The machete stands for farm work, the cog for factory work.
ao.fun: The Angolan desert is home to the welwitschia, a plant that grows just two leaves in its whole life and can live over a thousand years.

al.flag: A red field with a black double-headed eagle. The same eagle was on the seal of Skanderbeg, the leader who defended the country in the 1400s.
al.fun: In Albanian the country is Shqipëri, a name linked to the word for eagle: Albanians call their land the country of eagles.

ae.flag: Green, white and black stripes with a red vertical band at the hoist — the four pan-Arab colours found on many Arab flags.
ae.fun: In the mid-20th century the place where Dubai's skyscrapers now stand was sand and fishing villages, and the main trade was pearl diving.

ar.flag: Light blue, white and light blue stripes with the Sun of May in the middle — a sun with a human face, the sign of independence.
ar.fun: Argentina is so long that one end has hot desert and the other has glaciers you can walk right up to.

am.flag: Red, blue and orange stripes. The orange band is usually explained as the colour of work and wheat fields.
am.fun: Armenian lavash bread is baked by slapping thin dough onto the hot wall of a tonir, an oven sunk into the ground.

aq.flag: A blue field with the white outline of the continent. It is not a state flag: Antarctica has no country, and the design was made for shared use.
aq.fun: All the meridians meet at the South Pole, so you can walk around the flag there and cross every time zone in a few steps.

tf.flag: A blue field with the French flag in the corner, the white letters TF and the stars of the Southern Cross.
tf.fun: Nobody lives here permanently, only researchers at the stations — but there are hundreds of thousands of penguins and seals.

au.flag: A blue field with the British flag in the corner, the big seven-pointed Commonwealth Star and the Southern Cross.
au.fun: Australia put the kangaroo and the emu on its coat of arms because neither animal can walk backwards.

at.flag: Red, white and red stripes — one of the oldest flag designs in Europe, known since the 13th century.
at.fun: Legend says the pattern came from a battle: the duke's coat was soaked red except for the strip under his belt.

az.flag: Blue, red and green stripes with a white crescent and an eight-pointed star in the middle.
az.fun: In Azerbaijan natural gas seeps out of the ground and burns for centuries, which is why it is called the land of fire.

bi.flag: A white diagonal cross splits the flag into red and green parts, with three red stars in a white disc in the middle.
bi.fun: Lake Tanganyika on Burundi's border is the second deepest lake in the world, after Baikal.

be.flag: Black, yellow and red vertical stripes — the colours of the old Brabant coat of arms, a gold lion on black.
be.fun: Belgium gave the world Tintin and the Smurfs, and in Brussels comic characters are painted right onto house walls.

bj.flag: A green band at the hoist with yellow and red stripes beside it — the pan-African colours.
bj.fun: Benin has a town called Ganvié built entirely on stilts in a lake, where people travel between houses by boat.

bf.flag: Red and green bands with a yellow star in the middle.
bf.fun: The country's name means roughly “land of upright people”; it replaced the old colonial name in 1984.

bd.flag: A green field with a red disc set slightly towards the hoist, so it looks centred when the flag is flying.
bd.fun: Almost all of Bangladesh lies in a river delta, so part of the country goes under water every year in the floods.

bg.flag: White, green and red stripes: white for peace, green for fields and forests, red for courage.
bg.fun: Bulgarians grow whole fields of roses for rose oil — it takes thousands of blossoms to make a single drop.

bs.flag: Aquamarine and gold stripes for the sea and the sand, with a black triangle at the hoist.
bs.fun: One Bahamian island has pigs that swim in the sea and paddle out to meet the boats.

ba.flag: A blue field with a yellow triangle and a line of white stars. The triangle hints at the country's three peoples and at its shape.
ba.fun: In Mostar the old bridge is so high that locals dive from it into the river — an old tradition and a real competition.

by.flag: Red and green bands with a white woven pattern at the hoist, the kind embroidered on traditional towels.
by.fun: The Białowieża Forest is home to the wisent, Europe's heaviest wild animal, saved when almost none were left.

bz.flag: A blue field with red bands top and bottom and a coat of arms showing two woodcutters and a tree.
bz.fun: Off the coast of Belize lies the Great Blue Hole, an almost perfectly round sea sinkhole over 300 metres across.

bo.flag: Red, yellow and green stripes with the coat of arms in the middle. Bolivia also flies the wiphala, the chequered flag of its indigenous peoples.
bo.fun: After rain the Uyuni salt flat turns into a giant mirror, so you seem to be walking across the sky.

br.flag: A green field, a yellow diamond and a blue globe with stars and the motto “Order and Progress”. The stars show the sky over Rio on the night the republic was declared.
br.fun: Brazil borders almost every country in South America — all of them except Chile and Ecuador.

bn.flag: A yellow field with white and black diagonal stripes and a red emblem in the middle.
bn.fun: Brunei's capital has a whole district on the water, with houses, schools and shops on stilts above the river.

bt.flag: The flag is split diagonally into yellow and orange, with a white dragon clutching jewels across the middle.
bt.fun: Bhutan measures success by Gross National Happiness and by law must keep more than half the country under forest.

bw.flag: A light blue field with a black band edged in white. The blue stands for water, the most precious thing in a dry country.
bw.fun: The Okavango River never reaches the sea — it spreads across the desert into a huge swamp full of wildlife.

cf.flag: Four horizontal stripes crossed by a red vertical one, with a yellow star in the corner. The red band ties together the African and French colours.
cf.fun: Savannah and forest cover nearly the whole country, and there are so many rivers that travelling by water was once easier than by road.

ca.flag: Red bands at the sides and a red maple leaf in the middle. The leaf has eleven points — just a design, not a count of provinces.
ca.fun: Canada has a longer coastline than any other country: stretched out, it would wrap around the Earth several times.

ch.flag: A white cross on red. The Swiss flag is square — only one other country's flag is.
ch.fun: The other square flag belongs to Vatican City. And the Red Cross symbol is the Swiss flag reversed, honouring the country where it began.

cl.flag: White and red bands with a blue square and a white star at the hoist.
cl.fun: Chile is long and thin: you can drive across it in a couple of hours, but driving its length takes days.

cn.flag: A red field with one large yellow star and four smaller ones beside it.
cn.fun: All of China uses a single time zone, even though the country is so wide that the sun rises hours later in the west.

ci.flag: Orange, white and green vertical stripes — like the Irish flag, but with the colours in reverse order.
ci.fun: Côte d'Ivoire grows more cocoa than any other country: its beans are in almost every chocolate bar.

cm.flag: Green, red and yellow vertical stripes with a yellow star in the middle.
cm.fun: Cameroon is called “Africa in miniature”: one country holds desert, jungle, mountains and seashore.

cd.flag: A sky-blue field with a yellow star in the corner and a red diagonal band edged in yellow.
cd.fun: The Congo is the only big river that crosses the equator twice, so it always has water in it.

cg.flag: Green and red parts divided by a yellow diagonal band.
cg.fun: Rainforest covers nearly two thirds of the country — the second largest in the world after the Amazon.

co.flag: A yellow band filling the whole upper half, with blue and red below. Yellow is the country's gold, blue its two oceans, red the blood that was shed.
co.fun: Colombia has the Caño Cristales river: for a few weeks a year water plants turn it red, yellow and green.

cr.flag: Five bands: blue, white, red, white and blue again. The red one in the middle is wider than the rest.
cr.fun: Costa Rica has had no army since 1948: it was disbanded and the money went to schools and hospitals.

cu.flag: Blue and white stripes with a red triangle at the hoist holding a white star. The three blue stripes are the parts the island was once divided into.
cu.fun: Cuba still runs American cars from the 1950s, kept alive by decades of repairs because new ones were long impossible to buy.

cy.flag: A white field with a copper-yellow outline of the island itself and two olive branches for peace.
cy.fun: The word for copper in many languages comes from the name of Cyprus: the island was famous for its copper mines in ancient times.

cz.flag: White and red bands with a blue triangle at the hoist. The blue was added so the flag would not be confused with Poland's.
cz.fun: The city of Plzeň gave its name to a whole kind of beer — pilsner, now brewed all over the world.

de.flag: Black, red and gold from top to bottom. These were the colours worn by volunteers who fought against Napoleon.
de.fun: Germany gave the world printing with movable type and the kindergarten — a word other languages borrowed without translating.

dj.flag: Light blue and green bands with a white triangle at the hoist holding a red star.
dj.fun: Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa, and its water is several times saltier than the sea.

dk.flag: A white cross on red, shifted towards the hoist. The Dannebrog is considered the oldest national flag still in use.
dk.fun: Legend says it fell from the sky during a battle in 1219; every Nordic flag follows the Danish cross.

do.flag: A white cross divides the flag into blue and red quarters, with a coat of arms in the middle showing a cross and an open book.
do.fun: The Dominican Republic is the only country with a Bible on its flag.

dz.flag: Green and white halves with a red crescent and star in the middle.
dz.fun: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, and more than four fifths of it is Sahara.

ec.flag: A yellow band half the height of the flag, blue and red below, and a coat of arms with a condor and Mount Chimborazo.
ec.fun: The summit of Chimborazo is the farthest point from the centre of the Earth — farther than Everest, because the planet bulges at the equator.

eg.flag: Red, white and black stripes with the golden Eagle of Saladin in the middle.
eg.fun: The pyramids at Giza were already ancient in Cleopatra's day: more time separates her from their building than separates us from her.

er.flag: A red triangle running the length of the flag, green above and blue below, with a golden olive branch and wreath at the hoist.
er.fun: Asmara has kept a whole city of 1930s Italian architecture, now on the World Heritage list.

es.flag: Red, yellow and red bands, the middle one twice as wide. The yellow band carries a coat of arms with a crown and two columns.
es.fun: The columns are the Pillars of Hercules by Gibraltar, and the ribbon around them means “further beyond”.

ee.flag: Blue, black and white stripes, chosen by students in the 19th century: blue for sky and lakes, black for the soil, white for snow.
ee.fun: Estonia was the first country in the world to let people vote in elections over the internet.

et.flag: Green, yellow and red bands with a blue disc and a golden star. Many African countries later took up these three colours.
et.fun: Ethiopia keeps its own calendar: it has thirteen months and runs about seven years behind the usual one.

fi.flag: A blue cross on white: blue for the lakes, white for the snow.
fi.fun: Finland has about 188,000 lakes — roughly one for every thirty people.

fj.flag: A light blue field with the British flag in the corner and a shield showing sugar cane, a palm, bananas and a dove.
fj.fun: Fiji is made of about 330 islands, but people live on only a third of them.

fk.flag: A blue field with the British flag in the corner and a coat of arms showing a ram and a sailing ship.
fk.fun: The Falklands have many times more sheep than people — and even more penguins than sheep.

fr.flag: Three vertical stripes: blue, white and red. Blue and red are the colours of Paris, white was the king's colour.
fr.fun: The metre was first defined in France as one forty-millionth of the Earth's circumference through the poles.

ga.flag: Green, yellow and blue bands: the forest, the equator and the sea.
ga.fun: National parks cover more than a tenth of Gabon, and elephants and hippos wander its beaches and swim in the ocean.

gb.flag: Three crosses combined in one flag: St George's for England, St Andrew's for Scotland and St Patrick's for Ireland.
gb.fun: The flag is not symmetrical: the white stripes beside the diagonals differ in width, so it can be flown upside down.

ge.flag: A white field with a large red cross and four small crosses in the corners, going back to medieval banners.
ge.fun: Georgians make wine in clay qvevri buried in the ground — and have done so for about eight thousand years.

gh.flag: Red, gold and green bands with a black star in the middle. The black star became a symbol of African freedom.
gh.fun: Ghana was the first African colony south of the Sahara to become independent, in 1957.

gn.flag: Red, yellow and green vertical stripes — the pan-African colours.
gn.fun: Three of West Africa's great rivers, the Niger among them, all rise in the mountains of Guinea.

gm.flag: Red, blue and green bands separated by white lines. The blue is the Gambia River, along which the country stretches.
gm.fun: The Gambia is mainland Africa's smallest country, a narrow ribbon along both banks of its river.

gw.flag: A red band at the hoist with a black star, and yellow and green bands beside it.
gw.fun: Off the coast lies the Bijagós archipelago, home to hippos that swim in salty sea water.

gq.flag: Green, white and red bands, a blue triangle at the hoist and a coat of arms with a silk-cotton tree.
gq.fun: It is the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.

gr.flag: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in the corner. The nine stripes are linked to the syllables of an old freedom motto.
gr.fun: Greece is made of thousands of islands, but people live on fewer than three hundred of them.

gl.flag: White and red halves with a disc coloured the other way round: red on top, white below — the sun above the ice.
gl.fun: Greenland is the largest island in the world, and almost all of it lies under ice kilometres thick.

gt.flag: Blue, white and blue vertical bands with a coat of arms in the middle showing a quetzal bird.
gt.fun: The quetzal is not only the bird on the arms but also the money: Guatemalans pay in quetzales.

gy.flag: A green field with a yellow arrowhead and a red triangle at the hoist. The flag is nicknamed the Golden Arrowhead.
gy.fun: Kaieteur Falls drops in a single sheet almost four times higher than Niagara.

hn.flag: Blue, white and blue bands, with five blue stars on the white — the five countries that once formed a single federation.
hn.fun: Honduras gets a “rain of fish”: after heavy downpours people find live fish on the ground.

hr.flag: Red, white and blue bands with a coat of arms in the middle showing a red and white chequerboard.
hr.fun: The necktie was invented in Croatia: the French called it cravate after the word for Croat.

ht.flag: Blue and red bands with a white square in the middle holding the arms: a palm tree, cannons and flags.
ht.fun: Haiti was the first country where enslaved people rose up, won, and founded a state of their own.

hu.flag: Red, white and green bands: strength, faithfulness and hope.
hu.fun: Hungarian is not related to its neighbours' languages: its closest relatives are Finnish and Estonian, and even those are distant.

id.flag: A red band above a white one. Monaco's flag looks the same — only the proportions differ.
id.fun: Indonesia is made of more than 17,000 islands, where hundreds of different languages are spoken.

in.flag: Saffron, white and green bands, with a blue 24-spoked wheel on the white — the Ashoka Chakra, a sign of motion and law.
in.fun: India gave the world the digit zero and chess, which grew out of the ancient game of chaturanga.

ie.flag: Green, white and orange vertical stripes. The white between them stands for peace between two communities.
ie.fun: Ireland has no wild snakes: legend credits St Patrick, but really they never made it back after the Ice Age.

ir.flag: Green, white and red bands with a red emblem in the middle and an inscription repeated many times along the edges of the white band.
ir.fun: The Persian new year, Nowruz, falls on the spring equinox, and the table is set with seven items whose names all start with the same letter.

iq.flag: Red, white and black bands with a green Arabic inscription on the white one.
iq.fun: In Mesopotamia, where Iraq is today, the first known writing appeared — cuneiform pressed into clay tablets.

is.flag: A blue field with a red cross edged in white: blue for the sea, white for ice, red for volcanic fire.
is.fun: In Iceland almost every home is heated with hot water straight from the ground.

il.flag: A white field with two blue stripes and a blue six-pointed Star of David. The stripes recall the tallit prayer shawl.
il.fun: The Dead Sea is so salty that you cannot sink in it: a person floats like a cork.

it.flag: Green, white and red vertical stripes, inspired by Napoleon's tricolour with the blue swapped for green.
it.fun: Italy is shaped like a boot, and the island of Sicily sits at its toe like a ball.

jm.flag: A gold diagonal cross splits the flag into green and black parts. It is the only national flag with no red, white or blue.
jm.fun: Jamaica is the home of reggae, and its bobsled team once went to the Winter Olympics from an island that never sees snow.

jo.flag: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist holding a white seven-pointed star.
jo.fun: The city of Petra is carved straight into rose-coloured cliffs, its temples cut from the rock over two thousand years ago.

jp.flag: A white field with a red disc — the rising sun. The country's name means exactly that: origin of the sun.
jp.fun: Japan has more than 6,800 islands, and its trains are so punctual that a one-minute delay counts as an incident.

kz.flag: A sky-blue field with a golden sun and a steppe eagle beneath it, and a national ornament along the hoist.
kz.fun: Kazakhstan is the largest country in the world with no access to the ocean.

ke.flag: Black, red and green bands separated by white lines, with a Maasai shield and two spears in the middle.
ke.fun: Kenyan runners win more marathons than anyone else; many grew up in highlands over two kilometres above the sea.

kg.flag: A red field with a yellow forty-rayed sun, and in its middle the tunduk, the wooden crown at the top of a yurt.
kg.fun: The forty rays are the forty tribes united by the hero Manas, whose epic is one of the longest in the world.

kh.flag: Blue bands top and bottom, red in the middle, and on it the white temple of Angkor Wat — the only flag whose main image is a real building.
kh.fun: Angkor Wat is the largest religious building in the world, put up about 900 years ago.

kr.flag: A white field with the red and blue taegeuk circle in the middle and four black trigram symbols in the corners.
kr.fun: The Korean alphabet hangul was designed so anyone could learn to read: its letters show how the mouth and tongue are shaped.

xk.flag: A blue field with the gold outline of the territory and six white stars above it.
xk.fun: This is one of Europe's youngest states: independence was declared in 2008.

kw.flag: Green, white and red bands with a black trapezoid at the hoist — the pan-Arab colours.
kw.fun: Kuwait is almost all desert, and much of its drinking water comes from taking the salt out of sea water.

la.flag: Red bands top and bottom, blue in the middle and a white disc — the moon over the Mekong.
la.fun: Laos is the only country in Southeast Asia with no sea coast, but the Mekong runs right through it.

lb.flag: Red bands top and bottom, white in the middle, and on it a green Lebanon cedar.
lb.fun: Lebanon's cedars were already growing in the time of the pharaohs, who used them for ships and temples.

lr.flag: Eleven red and white stripes and a blue square with a single white star. It resembles the American flag because settlers from the USA founded the country.
lr.fun: A huge number of the world's ships fly the Liberian flag, because it is easier for owners to register them there.

ly.flag: Red, black and green bands, with a white crescent and star on the black.
ly.fun: Libya is nearly all desert, and beneath it lies a vast store of ancient groundwater piped right across the country.

lk.flag: A dark red field with a golden lion holding a sword, four bo leaves in the corners, and green and orange bands at the hoist.
lk.fun: Sri Lanka is a leading tea producer; the crop took over after disease destroyed the island's coffee plantations.

ls.flag: Blue, white and green bands with a black mokorotlo straw hat in the middle.
ls.fun: Lesotho is surrounded entirely by one country, South Africa, and all of its land lies over a kilometre above sea level.

lt.flag: Yellow, green and red bands: sun and fields, forests, blood and courage.
lt.fun: Lithuania is called the land of amber — hardened resin from trees tens of millions of years old, found for centuries along the Baltic shore.

lu.flag: Red, white and light blue bands. It differs from the Dutch flag by its lighter blue.
lu.fun: Luxembourg is the world's only grand duchy, and public transport across the whole country is free.

lv.flag: A dark red field with a narrow white band across the middle. The shade is known as Latvian red.
lv.fun: Riga claims to be the city where the first public Christmas tree was decorated.

ma.flag: A red field with a green five-pointed star drawn as one interlaced line.
ma.fun: In Morocco goats climb argan trees and eat the fruit straight off the branches.

mc.flag: A red band above a white one — almost the same as Indonesia's, only shorter.
mc.fun: Monaco is under two square kilometres: you can walk across the whole country in less than an hour.

md.flag: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands with an eagle in the middle, a cross in its beak and an aurochs head on its shield.
md.fun: Moldova has wine cellars tens of kilometres long — people drive through them by car.

mg.flag: A white band at the hoist with red and green bands beside it.
mg.fun: Nine out of ten of Madagascar's animals and plants live nowhere else: the island broke away from the mainland long ago.

mx.flag: Green, white and red bands, with arms on the white: an eagle on a cactus holding a snake in its beak.
mx.fun: Legend says the Aztecs founded their city where they saw that eagle — where Mexico City stands today.

mk.flag: A red field with a yellow sun whose eight broad rays reach the edges.
mk.fun: Lake Ohrid is millions of years old and holds fish found nowhere else on Earth.

ml.flag: Green, yellow and red vertical stripes.
ml.fun: Timbuktu was a city of scholars, holding tens of thousands of manuscripts — books were valued above gold.

mm.flag: Yellow, green and red bands with a large white star across them.
mm.fun: On Lake Inle fishermen row standing up with one leg, keeping their hands free for the net.

me.flag: A red field with a gold border and a crowned golden double-headed eagle in the middle.
me.fun: The country's name means “black mountain”, given by the Venetians for the dark forests on its slopes.

mn.flag: Red bands at the sides, blue in the middle, and the golden soyombo at the hoist — fire, sun, moon and other symbols.
mn.fun: Mongolia has roughly ten times more livestock than people, and one of the lowest population densities on Earth.

mz.flag: Green, black and yellow bands with a red triangle at the hoist holding a star, a book, a hoe and a rifle.
mz.fun: It is the only flag in the world showing a Kalashnikov rifle.

mr.flag: A green field with a gold crescent and star, and red bands top and bottom.
mr.fun: One of the world's longest trains runs across Mauritania: the ore train stretches more than two kilometres.

mw.flag: Black, red and green bands with a red rising sun on the black.
mw.fun: Lake Malawi holds more species of fish than any other lake in the world.

my.flag: Fourteen red and white stripes and a blue canton with a yellow crescent and a fourteen-pointed star, one point per part of the country.
my.fun: Malaysian forests grow the rafflesia, the world's largest flower — up to a metre across, and it smells of rotting meat.

na.flag: Blue and green parts split by a red diagonal band, with a golden rayed sun in the upper corner.
na.fun: The Namib is considered the oldest desert on Earth, and its coastal dunes are among the tallest anywhere.

nc.flag: Blue, red and green bands with a yellow disc holding the black roof-spear emblem of a traditional house. The French tricolour is flown alongside it here.
nc.fun: New Caledonia's lagoon is ringed by the second longest coral reef in the world, after the Great Barrier Reef.

ne.flag: Orange, white and green bands with an orange disc in the middle — the sun over the Sahara.
ne.fun: Niger is where skeletons of Sarcosuchus were found, giant crocodiles longer than a bus.

ng.flag: Green, white and green vertical bands: green for fields and forests, white for peace.
ng.fun: Nigeria makes so many films that its industry is nicknamed Nollywood, one of the largest in the world by number of titles.

ni.flag: Blue, white and blue bands with arms in the middle: a triangle, volcanoes and a rainbow.
ni.fun: Nicaragua has a freshwater lake with sharks in it — they swim up the river from the sea.

nl.flag: Red, white and blue bands. The top stripe was once orange, but the dye faded quickly in the sun.
nl.fun: More than a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, land won back from the water with dikes and pumps.

no.flag: A blue cross edged in white on red: Swedish colours set inside the Danish flag.
no.fun: In northern Norway the sun stays up for weeks in summer and never rises for weeks in winter.

np.flag: The world's only national flag that is not a rectangle: two pennants stacked together, bearing a white moon and sun.
np.fun: Nepal holds Everest and eight more of the world's fourteen highest peaks.

nz.flag: A blue field with the British flag in the corner and four red stars edged in white — the Southern Cross.
nz.fun: New Zealand is home to the kiwi, a wingless bird that lays an egg nearly a quarter of its own size.

om.flag: White, red and green bands with a red band at the hoist and the national emblem in the corner: a khanjar dagger over two swords.
om.fun: Oman traded frankincense for centuries, shipping the resin of rare trees to Egypt and Rome.

pk.flag: A green field with a white crescent and star, and a white band at the hoist standing for the country's religious minorities.
pk.fun: Pakistan has K2, the world's second highest peak and harder to climb than Everest.

pa.flag: The flag is quartered: white squares with a blue and a red star, plus a blue and a red one.
pa.fun: The Panama Canal joined two oceans; a ship crosses it in about half a day instead of sailing all the way around South America.

pe.flag: Red, white and red vertical bands. The coat of arms appears only on the state version of the flag.
pe.fun: The Inca built Machu Picchu without iron tools, wheels or mortar: the stones fit so tightly you cannot slip a blade between them.

ph.flag: Blue and red bands with a white triangle at the hoist holding a sun and three stars. In wartime the flag is flown upside down, red on top.
ph.fun: The Philippines is over seven thousand islands, nearly each with its own way of speaking.

pg.flag: The flag is split diagonally: the Southern Cross on the black half, a golden bird-of-paradise on the red.
pg.fun: Papua New Guinea has nearly 850 languages, more than any other country in the world.

pl.flag: A white band on top, red below. The colours come from the coat of arms: a white eagle on a red field.
pl.fun: Marie Skłodowska-Curie named the first element she discovered polonium, after Poland.

pr.flag: Red and white stripes with a blue triangle at the hoist holding a white star — like Cuba's, with the colours swapped.
pr.fun: Puerto Rico has bays that glow at night, lit by tiny organisms that flash when the water moves.

kp.flag: Blue bands top and bottom, a wide red band between them, and a red five-pointed star in a white disc.
kp.fun: North Korea counts years its own way, starting from the birth of the state's founder.

pt.flag: Green and red fields with an armillary sphere between them — an old navigator's instrument — and a shield with castles and smaller shields.
pt.fun: Portuguese sailors were the first from Europe to reach India around Africa, and Portuguese became a mother tongue on several continents.

py.flag: Red, white and blue bands with an emblem in the middle. This flag has a different emblem on the reverse — no other flag does.
py.fun: Almost everyone in Paraguay speaks Guaraní, an indigenous language that is as official as Spanish.

ps.flag: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist — the pan-Arab colours.
ps.fun: Jericho is considered one of the oldest cities where people have lived without a break for over ten thousand years.

qa.flag: A maroon field with a white band at the hoist ending in nine saw-like points.
qa.fun: Qatar is a desert peninsula with almost no rivers, but some of the world's largest gas reserves.

ro.flag: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands. It differs from Chad's flag by a slightly lighter blue.
ro.fun: Romania has Bran Castle, tied to the Dracula story, though the real prince Vlad hardly ever lived there.

ru.flag: White, blue and red bands. This tricolour was flown on the first Russian ships back in the 17th century.
ru.fun: Russia is so wide that it spans eleven time zones: when people go to bed at one end, they are having breakfast at the other.

rw.flag: Blue, yellow and green bands with a golden rayed sun in the upper corner.
rw.fun: Rwanda's mountains are home to mountain gorillas, among the rarest large animals on Earth.

eh.flag: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist and a red crescent and star in the middle.
eh.fun: Western Sahara is almost entirely desert, with fewer people than live in a single large city.

sa.flag: A green field with a white Arabic inscription and a sword beneath it. This flag is never flown at half-mast, because the words are held sacred.
sa.fun: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers at all: its water is either underground or desalinated from the sea.

sd.flag: Red, white and black bands with a green triangle at the hoist.
sd.fun: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt — around two hundred of them, narrower and more steeply sloped.

ss.flag: Black, red and green bands separated by white lines, with a blue triangle at the hoist holding a gold star.
ss.fun: South Sudan is the world's youngest country, created in 2011.

sn.flag: Green, yellow and red vertical bands with a green star in the middle.
sn.fun: Lake Retba near Dakar is so salty that algae living in it turn the water pink.

sb.flag: Blue and green parts split by a yellow diagonal band, with five white stars in the upper corner.
sb.fun: The Solomon Islands have nurse sharks and saltwater crocodiles, and water so clear you can see the bottom tens of metres down.

sl.flag: Green, white and blue bands: the land, peace and the sea.
sl.fun: Sierra Leone produced one of the largest diamonds ever found, the Star of Sierra Leone, over 900 carats.

sv.flag: Blue, white and blue bands with arms in the middle: a triangle, volcanoes and a rainbow.
sv.fun: El Salvador is called the land of volcanoes: it has a couple of dozen, many visible from the cities.

so.flag: A light blue field with a white five-pointed star. The colour came from the UN flag, and the points stand for Somali lands.
so.fun: Somalia has the longest coastline of any country on mainland Africa.

rs.flag: Red, blue and white bands with the coat of arms towards the hoist: a double-headed eagle and a shield with four firesteels.
rs.fun: Nikola Tesla came from a Serbian family, and the unit of magnetic field strength is named after him.

sr.flag: Green, white and red bands with a yellow star in the middle.
sr.fun: Suriname is the smallest country in South America, and over nine tenths of it is rainforest.

sk.flag: White, blue and red bands with the arms towards the hoist: a double cross on three hills.
sk.fun: Slovakia has over a hundred surviving castles — one of the densest collections anywhere for so small a country.

si.flag: White, blue and red bands with arms towards the hoist showing the outline of Mount Triglav and waves.
si.fun: Over half of Slovenia is forest, and the word “karst” comes from the Kras region, where such caves were first studied.

se.flag: A yellow cross on blue, shifted towards the hoist like every Nordic flag.
se.fun: Sweden gave the world safety matches and the three-point seatbelt, whose patent was handed to everyone for free.

sz.flag: Blue bands top and bottom, red in the middle, bearing an Nguni shield with spears and a staff.
sz.fun: Eswatini changed its name in 2018: the old name, Swaziland, was too often confused with Switzerland.

sy.flag: Green, white and black bands with three red stars in the middle. This flag became the national one only recently.
sy.fun: Damascus is among the longest continuously inhabited cities: the streets of its old town have kept their layout for a thousand years.

td.flag: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands — almost identical to Romania's, but with a darker blue.
td.fun: Lake Chad has shrunk many times over in half a century, its shore pulling back by tens of kilometres.

tg.flag: Five green and yellow stripes with a red square and a white star in the corner.
tg.fun: Togo is one of Africa's narrowest countries: a single road runs from the ocean to its northern border.

th.flag: Red and white bands with a wide blue one in the middle: the people, the faith and the king.
th.fun: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never a European colony.

tj.flag: Red, white and green bands, with a gold crown and seven stars on the white.
tj.fun: Mountains cover more than nine tenths of Tajikistan; in the Pamirs the roads climb above four kilometres.

tm.flag: A green field with a crescent and five stars, and a carpet band at the hoist showing the five main tribal patterns.
tm.fun: In the Karakum desert a gas crater has burned for over half a century; people call it the door to hell.

tl.flag: A red field with a yellow triangle at the hoist, a black one over it, and a white star in the black.
tl.fun: Timor-Leste is one of Asia's youngest countries: its independence was recognised in 2002.

tt.flag: A red field with a black diagonal band edged in white: fire, earth and water.
tt.fun: Trinidad has a lake of natural asphalt: you can walk on it, and the tar is shipped out for roads around the world.

tn.flag: A red field with a white disc holding a red crescent and star.
tn.fun: Desert-planet scenes for Star Wars were filmed in Tunisia, and some of the sets still stand in the sand.

tr.flag: A red field with a white crescent and a five-pointed star.
tr.fun: Istanbul sits on two continents at once: part of the city is in Europe, part in Asia, with a strait between them.

tw.flag: A red field with a blue canton holding a white sun of twelve rays — the twelve hours of the old way of counting time.
tw.fun: Taiwan makes most of the world's most advanced microchips: there is one in almost every phone.

tz.flag: Green and blue parts split by a black diagonal band edged in yellow.
tz.fun: Tanzania has Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, with snow on its summit almost at the equator.

ug.flag: Six black, yellow and red bands with a grey crowned crane in a white disc.
ug.fun: The Nile, Africa's longest river, flows out of Lake Victoria in Uganda.

ua.flag: A blue band on top, yellow below: the sky above a wheat field.
ua.fun: Beneath Odesa run catacombs over two thousand kilometres long — the largest network of underground passages in the world.

uy.flag: Nine white and blue stripes with the Sun of May in a white canton. The nine stripes are the regions the country began with.
uy.fun: Uruguay won the very first football World Cup, which it hosted itself in 1930.

us.flag: Thirteen stripes for the first colonies and fifty stars for today's states, added one by one as the country grew.
us.fun: The current fifty-star design was made by a schoolboy for a class project, and his teacher first gave it a poor grade.

uz.flag: Blue, white and green bands with red lines, and a crescent with twelve stars in the corner.
uz.fun: Samarkand and Bukhara stood on the Silk Road, passing silk, paper and glass between China and Europe.

ve.flag: Yellow, blue and red bands, with eight white stars arcing across the blue.
ve.fun: Angel Falls is the highest waterfall in the world: the water drops almost a kilometre and turns to mist on the way.

vn.flag: A red field with a large yellow five-pointed star.
vn.fun: Nearly two thousand limestone rock islands rise out of the water in Ha Long Bay.

vu.flag: Red and green parts, a black triangle at the hoist and a yellow shape like a sideways Y, with a boar's tusk in the triangle.
vu.fun: On Pentecost Island men jump from wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles — the custom that bungee jumping grew from.

ye.flag: Red, white and black bands — the pan-Arab colours with no emblem at all.
ye.fun: Yemen's island of Socotra grows dragon's blood trees shaped like open umbrellas, and almost a third of its plants live nowhere else.

za.flag: A green sideways Y edged in white and gold, with red, blue and black parts around it. Six colours — more than any other national flag.
za.fun: South Africa has three capitals at once: the government in Pretoria, parliament in Cape Town and the high court in Bloemfontein.

zm.flag: A green field with red, black and orange stripes at the fly and an orange eagle above them.
zm.fun: Victoria Falls thunders on Zambia's border; its spray is visible twenty kilometres away, so locals call it the smoke that thunders.

zw.flag: Seven stripes with a white triangle at the hoist holding a red star and the Zimbabwe Bird.
zw.fun: The bird copies carvings found at Great Zimbabwe, an ancient city built of stone without any mortar.

va.flag: A square flag: yellow and white halves, with crossed keys and a tiara on the white.
va.fun: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world — under half a square kilometre, entirely inside Rome.

sm.flag: White and light blue bands with a coat of arms in the middle showing three towers on three peaks.
sm.fun: San Marino calls itself the world's oldest republic, founded by tradition in the year 301.

li.flag: Blue and red bands with a gold crown in the upper corner, added after the 1936 Olympics revealed the flag matched Haiti's.
li.fun: Liechtenstein is one of only two countries surrounded entirely by other landlocked countries.

ad.flag: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands with a coat of arms in the middle.
ad.fun: Andorra is ruled jointly by two people — the president of France and a Spanish bishop — an arrangement kept since the 13th century.

mt.flag: White and red vertical halves with a grey George Cross edged in red in the upper corner.
mt.fun: Malta has temples older than the Egyptian pyramids, around five and a half thousand years old.

nr.flag: A blue field with a yellow stripe for the equator and a white twelve-pointed star below it: the island lies just south of the line.
nr.fun: Nauru is the smallest republic in the world; you can drive right around the island in under an hour.

tv.flag: A light blue field with the British flag in the corner and nine yellow stars, one for each island.
tv.fun: Tuvalu earns money from its internet address .tv, rented by television channels and websites worldwide.

pw.flag: A light blue field with a yellow disc set towards the hoist — the moon over the ocean.
pw.fun: Palau has a lake full of jellyfish that have all but lost their sting: with no predators there, people are allowed to swim in it.

mh.flag: A blue field with two widening diagonal bands, orange and white, and a white star of 24 points.
mh.fun: Marshall Islanders made charts from sticks and shells that showed not the islands but the way the waves run.

fm.flag: A light blue field with four white stars, one for each part of the country.
fm.fun: On Pohnpei stands Nan Madol, a city built across a hundred artificial islets made of stacked basalt logs.

ws.flag: A red field with a blue canton holding the Southern Cross in five white stars.
ws.fun: In 2011 Samoa skipped a whole day: the country crossed the date line, so 30 December simply never happened there.

to.flag: A red field with a white canton bearing a red cross.
to.fun: Tonga is the only country in Oceania that never lost its independence and is still ruled by a king.

ki.flag: A red upper half with a golden sun and a frigatebird above it, and blue and white waves below.
ki.fun: Kiribati stretches across every hemisphere at once, and is among the first places in the world to greet the New Year.

kn.flag: Green and red parts split by a black diagonal band edged in yellow, with two white stars on the band.
kn.fun: It is the smallest country in the Americas, both by area and by population.

gd.flag: A red border with six stars, yellow and green triangles, a star in a disc at the centre and a nutmeg at the hoist.
gd.fun: Grenada is called the spice island: its nutmeg even made it onto the flag.

vc.flag: Blue, yellow and green vertical bands, with three green diamonds on the yellow arranged as a V.
vc.fun: Pirates of the Caribbean was filmed here, and some of the sets still stand on the island.

bb.flag: Blue, yellow and blue vertical bands with a broken black trident in the middle.
bb.fun: The trident is broken on purpose: it marks the break with the colonial past.

ag.flag: A red field with a V shape in the middle made of black, blue and white bands, and a golden rising sun.
ag.fun: Antigua is said to have so many beaches that you could swim at a different one every day of the year.

lc.flag: A blue field with a black triangle edged in white and a yellow triangle in front of it — the Piton mountains above the sea.
lc.fun: The Pitons rise straight out of the sea: they are the hardened remains of ancient volcanoes.

mv.flag: A red field with a green rectangle in the middle holding a white crescent.
mv.fun: The Maldives is the flattest country in the world: almost all its land rises less than two metres above the sea.

sc.flag: Five rays fan out from the lower hoist corner: blue, yellow, red, white and green.
sc.fun: The Seychelles grows the coco de mer, the largest seed in the world, weighing up to twenty kilograms.

sg.flag: Red and white bands with a white crescent and five stars in a circle in the corner.
sg.fun: Singapore is a single city with a few islets, and remains one of the world's very few city-states.

bh.flag: A white band at the hoist and a red field, with a five-pointed zigzag between them for the five pillars of Islam.
bh.fun: Bahrain is an island joined to the mainland by a causeway about 25 kilometres long.
